page: Amazon Web Services g5g.8xlarge is an ARM64-based server powered by AWS Graviton processors utilizing the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz, with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The memory configuration consists of 64.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB per core. For graphics and accelerated workloads, it includes a single NVIDIA Turing T4G GPU with 16 GB of VRAM. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps, with no local NVMe storage bundled.

Performance benchmarks place the g5g.8xlarge in the average tier for most multi-core and database operations. The server achieved a multi-core Geekbench score of 11551.0 and a multi-core stress-ng CPU performance of 48574.86. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scoring 952.0 and text processing scoring 1232.0, both categorized as weak. Memory performance also shows divergence, with a strong read-only small block bandwidth of 1892.97 GB/sec, but a weak Passmark memory score of 1813.51.

The inclusion of the NVIDIA T4G GPU makes this instance class a cost-efficient option for ARM-native graphics-intensive workloads, Android game streaming, and entry-level machine learning. In LLM inference, it processes 15.24 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model, though text generation on smaller models drops to a poor rating of 42.38 tokens/sec. Given the dedicated ARM64 cores and GPU acceleration, it is best suited for containerized microservices, static web serving, and GPU-accelerated ARM applications, rather than single-threaded or memory-heavy database tasks.
